_why: Stack 1 of 4 (ruling 2026-08-08-inference-proxy-is-a-rules-stack): 'a stack for providers, listing their costs, connection handling, etc.' Shareable RULES only — machine facts (this LAN's endpoints, API keys) live in ~/.cairn/inference/hosts.json, never in git. Costs are AUTHORED numbers and therefore a labeled hypothesis (Law 3): the horizon is the first measured divergence between this table and the meter already in domain.resolve's door.
cost_units: cash_per_mtoken (USD per million tokens, authored first cut); measured latency is recorded as evidence beside it, not folded into the number

providers.name: hex
providers.connection: ollama HTTP API (/api/generate, /api/embed) over the local LAN; endpoint from the instance overlay
providers.cost_note: owned hardware (the Apple M1 Studio 32) — marginal cash per token is zero; the purchase price is metered separately by the Hex payback thread, which reads this domain's meter
providers.why: the ruling: 'That's what the inference proxy should usually route to.' Measured 2026-08-08: generate 1.39s on llama3.2:3b, 8x faster than this box's CPU on its smallest model; ollama 0.30.11.

providers.name: ollama-cloud
providers.connection: ollama's hosted service, keyed; API surface to be confirmed against their docs when the key lands (ollama-protocol-with-key assumed)
providers.cost_note: authored placeholder — no key, no measured calls; corrected from their price sheet the day the rung goes live
providers.why: the ruling: first failover when Hex does not answer. Listed and loudly refusing until a key reaches ~/.cairn/inference/ — an unkeyed rung is dead, not invisible.

providers.name: gemini
providers.connection: Google Gemini API, keyed, distinct request shape (not ollama protocol) — the resolver grows a gemini transport when the key lands, not before
providers.cost_note: authored placeholder — no key, no measured calls
providers.why: the ruling: second failover, behind Ollama Cloud.

providers.name: openrouter
providers.cost_note: not authored — a disabled rung gets no number to mislead with
providers.why: Akien, verbatim, 2026-08-08: 'We have OpenRouter, but I shut it off because bugs kept sucking up all the cash. That's why we now have Hex.' Re-enabling is his act, not a build's.

providers.name: loopback
providers.connection: this box's own ollama at 127.0.0.1:11434 (endpoint from the instance overlay)
providers.cost_note: cash-free but ruled out of routing regardless of cost — the rule is categorical, not economic
providers.why: the ruling: 'the lowest cost answer is NEVER 127.0.0.1.' Measured 2026-08-08: ~100s per 7B generate on this CPU-only box (Intel CometLake-U GT2) — the lived symptom this stack exists to end. Listed so the rule is a row a sieve reads, not a comment; routable never, by the never_route sieve.
